thread:
pagerbot: Pager duty triggered: high error rate for inference-serving-gpu-pool-us-west1. 45% of pods reporting transient GPU disconnects and host reboots in the last 7m. Severity: P1. Ticket: INC-2027-842. @sarah oncall

sarah: ACK-ing — pausing new deploys. I'm pulling logs and will triage. Who's on standby for customer comms?

devon: I can handle customer updates. Starting timeline aggregation.

mike: Seeing repeated PCIe AER messages on metrics and host logs. Pulling dmesg now.

mike: ```
[ 1234.567890] pcieport 0000:3c:00.0: AER: Multiple Corrected error received: id 00e0
[ 1234.567895] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3c:00): 79, pid=5123, name=python
[ 1234.568001] NVRM: GPU indicated to have a fault, resetting
[ 1238.001200] kernel: GPU ecc error: device 0000:3c:00.0
```

anita: Noted. Also seeing KV-cache misses spike and a lot of preempted inference jobs. That matches noisy neighbor symptoms.

kevin: Are these all from the same host family? i.e., same machine type/firmware?

mike: Most reboots come from host group gw-usw1-a (n1-ultra-8g-2024). Firmware version 2024.11.2 on most. Couple of nodes show older 2024.9.

sarah: Immediate mitigations: 1) cordon and drain affected nodes (devon/mike) 2) scale up warm spare pool to absorb traffic (infra autoscale policy) 3) open cloud provider support case with kernel + dmesg logs (kevin) 4) notify top 5 affected customers (devon)

devon: Starting drain on nodes: gw-usw1-a-12, -15, -18. Will shift traffic to dedicated spares.

mike: Drain done for the three nodes. Rolling restarts of pods succeeded for most routes, but some long-tail requests timed out.

cloud-support-bot: Cloud support case CS-98221 opened (GCP). Assigned to L3 networking/hw team. ETA initial response 30m. Attached logs: host-dmesg-2071234567.tar.gz

kevin: Sharing internal timeline so far: 
- T-07m: Pagerbot alerts (error rate > 30%)
- T-06m: First host reboot observed (gw-usw1-a-12)
- T-05m: 3 nodes rebooted within 90s window
- T-04m: PCIe AER and NVRM Xid 79 spikes in dmesg
- T-03m: Autoscaler started replacing drained capacity
- T-01m: Customer error rate down to 8% after spills

anita: Hypotheses (track):
- H1: Noisy tenant causing PCIe bus instability -> raises AER -> GPU resets.
- H2: Firmware/kernel regression interacting with this specific machine type -> causing ECC faults.
- H3: Intermittent PCIe fabric issues in GCP rack (cabling/host BMC flapping).

mike: On H1 — I can run gstack on top offender processes once we have one repro node. suspect an e2e load test job that does heavy GPU memory churn.

sarah: Important: preserve one repro node for deeper debug. Do NOT wipe until we snapshot logs and core. Kevin, can you request a memory/core dump from cloud support?

kevin: Filed request in CS-98221 for host core dump + nv-host logs. Also asked for PCIe link status, slot resets, and BMC alerts.

devon: Customer comms draft: "We're investigating increased GPU host resets affecting inference latency in us-west1. We've mitigated impact by draining affected hosts and scaling capacity. We're actively working with the cloud provider and will update within 60 minutes." Thoughts?

mike: LGTM. Add note about "possible noisy-tenant or host-level hardware issue" to set expectations.

anita: Sharing a quick grep of telemetry for ECC msgs from host logs:
```
$ zgrep -n "ECC error" /var/log/host-*.log
host-gw-usw1-a-12:123456:GPU ecc error: addr 0x7ff...
host-gw-usw1-a-15:123789:GPU ecc error: addr 0x2ab...
```

sarah: Ok, next actions:
- preserve one node for repro and enable increased log retention (mike)
- escalate to GCP with core dump request (kevin)
- keep customers updated (devon)
- build a short post-incident timeline and hypothesis tracker in this thread (me)

mike: Preserved gw-usw1-a-18 as repro node, increased /var/log retention, snapshotting nv-host logs to gs://redwood-incident-logs/2071234567/

cloud-support-bot: Update from GCP case CS-98221: "We see PCIe AER counts spike correlated with host flaps. Hardware team requested to inspect NIC/PCIe riser. Recommending isolate noisy VMs and test with known-good firmware."

kevin: GCP suggests isolating tenant VMs — does Redwood have tenant affinity mapping to hosts? If yes we can evict/evacuate suspect VMs.

anita: We currently run multi-tenant GPU pools in that zone for lower tiers. We have tenant -> host mapping logs. I'll run a query to identify high-util tenants on the affected hosts.

devon: For customer impact, I've queued messages to customers A, B, C (top 3) and will send an ops bulletin to the rest in 30m.

sarah: OK. We'll keep this thread as the canonical timeline/hypothesis tracker. Once cloud returns hardware findings we'll update H1/H2/H3. If GCP confirms noisy tenant, plan to shift to single-tenant warm pools and update infra policy.

mike: Quick note: I captured kernel oops on the preserved node, attaching snippet:
```
[ 2345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3c:00): 79, pid=7800, name=python
[ 2345.679012] nvidia 0000:3c:00.0: firmware: failed to load nv_fw.bin
[ 2345.679100] kernel: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Physical Layer, id=00e0
```

anita: Query results: tenant-id t-9143 had 6x higher GPU memcpy churn and launched large memory stress tests ~10m before incident. Likely candidate for noisy neighbor.

kevin: I'll coordinate an eviction of t-9143's VMs from the affected hosts and ask GCP to re-run PCIe stress tests post-eviction.

devon: Eviction scheduled, moving their workloads to warm-spares now. ETA 8m.

sarah: If eviction removes the spike and AER counts drop, we mark H1 as likely and then plan policy changes. If not, keep H2/H3 open.

cloud-support-bot: GCP update: after isolating suspect tenant on a test host, AER counts dropped to baseline. Hardware team still performing a physical check but initial trend points to noisy tenant-induced PCIe stress.

sarah: Summary for NOW: impact mitigated, customer error rate returned to baseline, GCP indicates noisy tenant likely root cause. Actions: follow-up RCA, infra policy to prefer single-tenant allocation for GPU pools in that zone, and expanded telemetry to detect PCIe AER early. Assigning RCA lead: anita.

anita: Will use this thread as evidence dump for RCA doc; will include logs, timelines, and steps for mitigation. I'll prep a short action item list and post an RCA draft in incidents/ after 24h.

mike: leaving repro node preserved until anita confirms we can release.

sarah: Thanks everyone. Closing pager for now, will reopen if noise returns. :white_check_mark:
